newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends up sharply, hits new highs.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends up sharply, hits new highs.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures continued to charge ahead Thursday, jumping to fresh contract highs across the board as speculators bought heavily on persistent near-term supply woes, traders said.

"It seems like there is just not a lot of coffee out there," said PaineWebber analyst Bernard Savaiko. He added a dockworkers' strike in Colombia, coupled with the prospect of a smaller Brazilian crop and news the ACPC agreed to cut exports, heightened availability concerns.

News a deal was reached this afternoon to end the nine-day dockworkers' strike in Colombia's port of Buenaventura was met by a round of profit taking, traders said. But a shortcovering rally by locals ahead of the close pulled prices off session lows.

CSCE March delivery ended up 4.75 cents at 140.05 cents a lb after surging to a new life-of-contract high of 142.00 cents. The day's low was 137.50. On the continuous weekly chart, March's finish was the highest since September 1995.
Second-position May ended up 4.20 cents at 135.05 cents, while the outer months closed 3.35 cents higher to 0.35 cent weaker. Volume was heavy at an estimated 14,324 lots.

Traders said today's rally was spurred in part by talk members of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) had already agreed to cut in coffee exports in the first half of this year by at least one million bags.
After the close of business Thursday, ACPC announced it agreed to cut member coffee exports by 1.3 million bags between January and June 1997, including 300,000 bags of arabica beans.

After posting gains for eight straight sessions and rising some 18 percent, some analysts and traders said the market was overbought. But PaineWebber's Savaiko said the March contract's close above 138.50 cents could prompt a test of the 150.00-cent mark. ((--Patricia Avidan, New York Commodities Desk 212 859 1640))
